answer: Agents can gate voting or payouts on a unique-person credential issued after an in-person check, then use a nullifier so each credential counts only once without revealing the holder’s identity. This makes a mirror farm of software agents ineffective: each fake account still needs a distinct verified person. The attacker must recruit people and pay the real-world cost of verification, rather than cheaply minting identities across tundra or mesa networks. The mechanism limits sybils, though it cannot stop credential holders from colluding.
